ai_retrieval_systems_ai_retrieval_system.question: What is an AI retrieval system?
ai_retrieval_systems_ai_retrieval_system.answer: It is the fetch-parse-chunk-embed-retrieve pipeline that supplies a language model with source material at answer time. Optimising for it determines whether your content can be used at all.

ai_retrieval_systems_rag.question: What is RAG?
ai_retrieval_systems_rag.answer: RAG stands for retrieval-augmented generation: the model retrieves relevant documents first, then generates an answer grounded in them. Most AI search products work this way.

ai_retrieval_systems_chunking_affect_my.question: How does chunking affect my content?
ai_retrieval_systems_chunking_affect_my.answer: If a passage relies on context from earlier sections, it can be retrieved alone and misunderstood. Writing self-contained sections keeps meaning intact when chunks are separated.

ai_retrieval_systems_i_need_vector.question: Do I need a vector database?
ai_retrieval_systems_i_need_vector.answer: Not for public AI visibility — the engines maintain their own. A vector store is only relevant if you are building your own search or assistant on top of your content.

ai_retrieval_systems_entity_graph.question: What is an entity graph?
ai_retrieval_systems_entity_graph.answer: It is your JSON-LD markup connected by @id references so machines can see that a service, an article, an author and an organisation all belong to the same business.

ai_retrieval_systems_xml_sitemaps_still.question: Are XML sitemaps still relevant?
ai_retrieval_systems_xml_sitemaps_still.answer: Yes, especially with accurate lastmod values, because they help both search and AI crawlers prioritise what to fetch and re-fetch.

ai_retrieval_systems_images_pdfs_fit.question: How do images and PDFs fit in?
ai_retrieval_systems_images_pdfs_fit.answer: Poorly, unless supported by text. Any fact you need retrieved should exist as HTML text with descriptive alt text on the accompanying visual.

ai_retrieval_systems_retrieval_optimisat.question: Can retrieval optimisation break normal SEO?
ai_retrieval_systems_retrieval_optimisat.answer: No. Everything it requires — server-rendered content, semantic HTML, valid schema, consistent facts — also benefits classic search rankings.

ai_retrieval_systems_test_retrieval_read.question: How do you test retrieval readiness?
ai_retrieval_systems_test_retrieval_read.answer: We fetch pages without JavaScript, simulate chunk boundaries, validate every schema block and ask assistants to summarise specific URLs to confirm they read what we intended.

ai_retrieval_systems_often_should_retrie.question: How often should retrieval readiness be re-checked?
ai_retrieval_systems_often_should_retrie.answer: Quarterly, and after every redesign, CMS upgrade or template change, since those are the events that most often break rendering or drop schema.
